ud2.8:2.3: ‘Sir, Suppavāsā the Koliyan bows with her head to your feet. She asks if you are healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.’
ud2.8:3.2: Seated to one side, the Koliyan gentleman said to the Buddha,
ud2.8:3.3: “Sir, Suppavāsā the Koliyan bows with her head to your feet, and asks if you are healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.
ud2.8:3.5: ‘Suppavāsā the Koliyan has been pregnant for seven years, and in obstructed labor for seven days.
ud2.8:3.6: While suffering painful, sharp, severe, acute feelings, three thoughts help her endure:
ud2.8:3.7: “Oh! The Blessed One is indeed a fully awakened Buddha, who teaches the Dhamma for giving up suffering such as this.
ud2.8:3.8: Oh! The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is indeed practicing well, who practice for giving up suffering such as this.
ud2.8:3.9: Oh! Extinguishment is so very blissful, where such suffering as this is not found.”’”
ud2.8:6.3: ‘Sir, Suppavāsā the Koliyan bows with her head to your feet.’
ud2.8:7.2: Seated to one side, the Koliyan gentleman said to the Buddha,
ud2.8:8.1: “Sir, Suppavāsā the Koliyan bows with her head to your feet.
ud2.8:8.3: ‘Suppavāsā the Koliyan, who was pregnant for seven years, and in obstructed labor for seven days,
ud2.8:8.4: is now happy and healthy and has given birth to a healthy child.
ud2.8:8.5: She invites the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha to a meal for seven days.
ud2.8:8.6: Sir, would the Buddha please accept seven meals from Suppavāsā?’”
ud2.8:10.2: “Suppavāsā the Koliyan, who was pregnant for seven years, and in obstructed labor for seven days,
ud2.8:10.3: is now happy and healthy and has given birth to a healthy child.
ud2.8:10.4: She invites the mendicant Saṅgha headed by the Buddha to a meal for seven days.
ud2.8:10.5: Let Suppavāsā make seven meals, afterwards you can make yours.”
